title.rendered: Come on Over to My Place

content.rendered:
In 1965, The Drifters had a hit with “Come on Over to My Place.” It only reached #60 on the charts in the US (it made it to #9 in the UK), but it was enough to make an impression on Bruce and Cats on a Smooth Surface–they played it together at The Stone Pony five times during the summer and fall of 1982.

Bruce and the Cats turned in a pretty faithful cover–listen to the original below for comparison.

Come On Over to My Place
First performed: August 1, 1982 (Asbury Park, NJ)
Last performed: October 3, 1982 (Asbury Park, NJ)

© April 12, 2018

excerpt.rendered: The Drifters’ classic makes frequent appearances at the Stone Pony in 1982.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rock Baby, Rock It
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Bruce Springsteen joins Stone Pony house band Cats on a Smooth Surface to cover a lost rockabilly classic.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Come On, Let’s Go
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bruce and Cats on a Smooth Surface cover Ritchie Valens' very first hit.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Ruby Baby
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Twice only: Bruce Springsteen and the E Street Band turn in steamy performances of "Ruby Baby" at The Stone Pony in the summer of 1987.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Under the Boardwalk
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bruce and Bobby cover "Under the Boardwalk" on the Jersey Shore on the third day of summer. There's no setting more perfect for that song.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Do You Want to Dance
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Listen to Bruce Springsteen join Rhode Island rockers Beaver Brown in a joyful cover of Bobby Freeman’s “Do You Want to Dance” in a surprise appearance in the summer of 1982.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rip It Up
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Twice only during the summer of 1982: Bruce covers "Rip It Up," Little Richard's #1 R&B 1956 hit, at back-to-back surprise club appearances.
